content:
Even if the price increase isn't as dramatic as initially expected, we anticipate that the all-new iPhone unveiled today will come with a price hike.

Reports indicate that Apple is offering higher trade-in valuations for devices with minor cosmetic damage, aiming to slightly ease the impact on some upgrade customers...

Apple already raised prices on most of its products back in June this year, with the iPhone escaping unscathed at the time. However, we expect the iPhone 18 Pro series launching today to be more expensive than its predecessor.

Earlier rumours suggested the iPhone price hike could be as much as US$200, but the latest reports indicate the increase will be around US$100. MacRumors now expects some upgrade customers to receive a bit more relief.

The report notes that the company will be more lenient with minor damage — for instance, a small crack on the screen glass will still qualify for the same trade-in valuation as a device in pristine condition. While this measure clearly aims to boost upgrade sales of the latest iPhone, the policy is expected to apply across the entire product line.

According to reports, the relevant changes will take effect immediately after the presentation ends and the Apple Store comes back online.

  • apple.com officially certified refurbished Apple products at 15% off
  • Official Apple Store on Amazon
  • AirPods Pro 3 discount offer
  • Adapter supporting wireless CarPlay
  • AirPod 10-year long-life battery protective case
  • Logitech MX Master 4 for Mac
